rationale: The buyer is a specific, named role — AI/ML engineers and platform leads at companies actively spending on LLM APIs — who already budget for observability tooling (Datadog, PagerDuty, etc.), giving strong willingness-to-pay signals. A canary-probing service can run largely automated: Claude runs scheduled eval prompts against provider APIs, detects quality regressions via scoring, and fires alerts with no per-customer human work. The deciding factor is that the pain is real (silent model degradation costs real money in broken pipelines) and the build is within reach — the core is a scheduler + eval harness + alert webhook, well within this factory's capabilities.
solution_plan: The micro-service is an LLM quality canary: it continuously sends standardized test prompts to Anthropic/OpenAI APIs and scores the responses, alerting customers when quality drops below their threshold. The factory builds it as a Claude-powered eval engine (scoring response quality on predefined rubrics), a simple signup page, a Stripe subscription link ($49–$99/mo), and a webhook/email alert system — no operator coding required. Customers are reached via direct outreach to AI engineers on HN, LinkedIn, and communities like the Anthropic Discord and Latent Space Slack; outreach batches go out only after operator approval. Once a customer connects their API keys via a form, delivery (running canary probes, scoring, alerting) runs fully via Claude + cron + email — the operator's only recurring touch is approving new outreach sends. The main risk is that larger teams may already use internal evals; positioning is for the long tail of teams with no dedicated MLOps.
notes: All build_gates met: operational_autonomy=7, buildability_with_ai=6, buyer_clarity=8, willingness_to_pay=7. Defensibility is moderate — first-mover distribution advantage matters here.
